headline: Gene-level and neighborhood-level inference methods for spatial omics datasets
label: Spatial Omics Quantitative Inference Methods
summary: Recent papers and preprints target fast querying, multiscale statistics, and gene-relationship inference directly on spatial omics data.
synthesis: The common thread is quantification at the level of individual genes, gene pairs, and local neighborhoods rather than global summaries of spatial data. Spectrast recasts spatial autocorrelation as FFT-based convolutions on rasterized expression matrices to yield multiscale per-gene statistics, while Spindle compresses spatial gene co-expression covariance matrices into a platform-agnostic searchable index for fast querying. GeneSPOT applies gene-centric optimal transport to measure how spatial gene relationships reorganize across conditions and time. Sphinx provides adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling with cell annotation and functional analysis, though it targets spatial proteomics rather than transcriptomics. The new element is treating spatial gene relationships and neighborhoods as explicit, testable objects, with scalability addressed directly in the indexing work.
